examples.en: The lamp on the desk is on.

examples.ko: 사람이 들어가면 복도 불이 저절로 켜져요.
examples.en: The hallway light turns on by itself when someone walks in.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터가 안 켜져서 수리 센터에 갔어요.
examples.en: My computer wouldn't turn on, so I went to the repair center.
The air conditioner came on by itself and I was startled.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 화면이 켜지지 않아요. 배터리가 없어요.
examples.en: My phone screen won't come on. The battery is dead.

explain: 켜다는 사람이 켜는 거고, 켜지다는 저절로 켜지거나 켜진 상태예요. 불, TV, 컴퓨터, 에어컨 모두 켜다와 켜지다를 써요. 반대말은 끄다와 꺼지다예요. 불이나 기계가 켜질 때 써요.

dict_examples.en: A fire was lit in the brazier.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The candles were lit and incense rose up.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 켜다 is turning something on yourself; 켜지다 is when it comes on by itself or is on. It works for lights, TVs, computers and air conditioners. The opposites are 끄다 and 꺼지다. Used for a light or machine.

examples.en: The light in the empty room is off.
My laptop suddenly shut off and I lost the file.
My phone turned off, so I couldn't get any calls or messages.
The candle went out in the wind.
The TV suddenly turned off, so I turned it back on.

explain: 전화가 안 될 때 “전화기가 꺼져 있어요”라고 해요. 배터리가 없을 때도 같아요. 사람이 끄면 끄다, 저절로 꺼지면 꺼지다예요. 불빛이나 기계가 꺼질 때 써요.

phrases.example: 외출하기 전에 가스 불을 한 번 더 봤어요. 꺼진 불도 다시 보자는 말이 있잖아요.
phrases.en: I checked the gas stove once more before going out. You know the saying: check even a fire that's already out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불조심 표어에서 온 말이에요. 끝난 것 같아도 한 번 더 확인하라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: comes from a fire-safety slogan; it means to check one more time even if something seems finished
phrases.en_equiv: I checked the gas stove once more before going out. You know the saying: check even a fire that's already out.

phrases.example: 밥을 먹고 좀 걸었더니 배가 꺼졌어요.
phrases.en: I walked a bit after eating, and now I don't feel full anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배부른 느낌이 없어지고 소화가 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: the full feeling is gone and the food has been digested
phrases.en_equiv: I walked a bit after eating, and now I don't feel full anymore.

explain_en: When a phone cannot be reached, you can say 전화기가 꺼져 있어요. The same goes for a dead battery. If a person turns it off it is 끄다; if it turns off by itself it is 꺼지다. It is used when a light or machine goes off.

en: to be placed; to feel relieved

examples.ko: 빨간 책이 책상 위에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A red book is lying on the desk.

examples.ko: 현관 앞에 택배 상자가 놓여 있었어요.
examples.en: A delivery box had been left at the front door.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나니까 베개 옆에 편지가 놓여 있었어요.
examples.en: When I woke up, a letter was lying next to my pillow.

examples.ko: 식탁 위에 맛있는 음식이 가득 놓였어요.
examples.en: The table was filled with delicious food.

examples.ko: 책이 책장 맨 위에 놓여 있어서 손이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: The book is on the top shelf, so I can't reach it.

explain: 사람이 놓으면 놓다, 물건이 놓인 상태는 놓이다예요. 물건의 위치를 설명할 때 “있어요” 대신 “놓여 있어요”라고 하면 더 자세하게 들려요.

dict_examples.ko: 우리 집 장롱에는 꽃무늬 자개가 놓였다.
dict_examples.en: A floral mother-of-pearl design was set into our wardrobe.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A person puts something down with 놓다; the state of the thing lying there is 놓이다. 놓여 있어요 sounds more descriptive than just 있어요 when you describe where something is.

en: to stick; to be attached; to cling

examples.en: There's a notice posted on the front of the door.
Gum got stuck to the bottom of my shoe.

examples.ko: 이 스티커는 오래돼서 잘 안 붙어요.
examples.en: This sticker is old, so it doesn't stick well.
A grain of rice is stuck on your face.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 붙은 메모를 보고 우유를 샀어요.
examples.en: I saw the note on the fridge and bought milk.

explain: 붙다는 둘이 딱 닿아서 떨어지지 않는 거예요. 저절로 붙으면 붙다, 사람이 붙이면 붙이다예요. 붙다는 [붇따]처럼 소리 나요.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 학교에서 항상 붙어 다녀요.
phrases.en: The two of them are always together at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늘 함께 다닐 만큼 친하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: so close that they go everywhere together
phrases.en_equiv: The two of them are always together at school.

phrases.en: With practice, I picked up speed when speaking.
phrases.nuance_en: to get used to something and gradually get faster
phrases.en_equiv: With practice, I picked up speed when speaking.

phrases.en: My older brother passed the university entrance exam this time.
phrases.nuance_en: to pass an exam; the opposite is '떨어지다'
phrases.en_equiv: My older brother passed the university entrance exam this time.

explain_en: Intransitive; something sticks by itself, like dust. 붙다 means two things touch and do not come apart. It sticks by itself with 붙다; a person sticks it with 붙이다. 붙다 sounds like [붇따].

p.n: 접착되다 is for glued bonding; it is not natural for dust on clothes.

t90.ax: A grain of rice is stuck on your face.

examples.ko: 탁상등이 켜져 있어서 책상 위가 밝아요.
examples.en: The desk lamp is on, so the desk is nice and bright.
I bought a desk lamp so I could read at night.
The desk lamp's light is warm, so it's nice for studying.

examples.ko: 잠들기 전에 탁상등만 켜고 책을 읽어요.
examples.en: Before I fall asleep, I turn on only the desk lamp and read.
My younger sibling fell asleep with the desk lamp on.

explain: 탁상은 책상 위, 등은 불이라는 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 “스탠드”라고도 많이 불러요.
explain_en: 탁상 means “on the desk” and 등 means “lamp”. In daily talk, people also very often call it a 스탠드.

examples.ko: 오른쪽 벽에 큰 액자가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A big picture frame is hanging on the right wall.

examples.ko: 졸업 사진을 액자에 넣어서 거실에 걸었어요.
examples.en: I framed my graduation photo and hung it in the living room.

examples.ko: 벽에 걸린 액자 속 사진이 우리 가족이에요.
examples.en: The photo in the frame on the wall is my family.

examples.ko: 친구 결혼 선물로 예쁜 액자를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pretty picture frame as a wedding gift for my friend.

examples.ko: 액자 유리가 깨져서 새 걸로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The glass in the frame broke, so I replaced it with a new one.

explain: 액자는 위치에 따라 동사가 달라요. 벽에는 “걸다”, 책상이나 선반 위에는 “세워 두다”라고 해요.
explain_en: The verb depends on where the frame goes. On a wall you hang it (걸다); on a desk or shelf you stand it up (세워 두다).

examples.ko: 뒷자리에 앉은 사람이 큰 소리로 말해요.
examples.en: The person in the back seat talks loudly.
It is hard to see from the back seat in the classroom.
I sat alone in the back seat of the bus.
The back seat was empty, so I moved over there.
Mom put the child in the back seat of the car.
The class was boring, so I talked with the friend in the back seat.

explain: '뒷좌석'은 주로 차 안에서 쓰고, 뒷자리는 교실·버스·극장까지 널리 써요. 반대말은 '앞자리'예요. 학교 이야기에서는 뒷자리가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The child sits in the back seat of the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷자리'와 같은 뜻이지만 주로 차 안에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 뒷자리, but mostly used inside a car.

phrases.en: I sat in the very back seat at the movie theater.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맨'을 붙이면 가장 뒤에 있는 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 맨 means the seat at the very back.

phrases.en: I came late, so I sat in a back seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앉는 동작을 말할 때 '에'를 붙여 '뒷자리에 앉다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 에 with the seat to say where you sit: 뒷자리에 앉다.
phrases.en_equiv: to sit in the back seat

explain_en: '뒷좌석' is mostly used inside a car, while 뒷자리 is used widely for classrooms, buses, and theaters too. The opposite is '앞자리'. In stories about school, 뒷자리 sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I sat alone in the back seat of the bus.

en: at a good distance; far off

examples.en: The puppy stands far away and looks at me.
I stepped well back to take a picture.

examples.ko: 불꽃놀이는 멀찍이 앉아서 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to watch fireworks from a seat some distance away.
He stepped far back and watched us.
I parked the car some distance away and walked.
The children threw the ball from a good distance away.

explain: '멀리'보다 '꽤 멀게 떨어져서'라는 느낌이고, 일부러 거리를 둔 것처럼 들릴 때가 많아요. '떨어지다, 서다, 물러나다, 앉다' 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요. '멀찌감치'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: The cat is sitting far away.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '멀찍이'; both are used.

phrases.en: When the car came, people stepped far back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤로 물러나 거리를 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when people step back to leave distance.

phrases.en: I had a fight with my friend, so I sat far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 거리를 두고 앉을 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when you sit apart on purpose.

explain_en: Compared with '멀리', it gives the feel of 'at a fair distance', and often sounds like keeping distance on purpose. It fits verbs such as 떨어지다, 서다, 물러나다 and 앉다. '멀찌감치' is used in a similar way.

t90.ax: He stepped far back and watched us.
